It is said
that after everything that was taken from him,
the wood, the charcoal, and the wine which remained in his courtyard, one of the grandees named Husayn ibn Mukhallad bought them for six thousand dinars,
and he sold them again for twelve thousand.
For this Bukhtisho bar Gabriel had transgressed against the ecclesiastical laws,
and had cohabited with two maidservants together.
And both of them conceived and bore two sons:
one Gabriel,
and the other John,
the one who became metropolitan of Mosul.
And from that time he prospered no more.
For formerly he used to sit in a carriage of ebony and go from the court of the Caliph to his own courtyard,
with about a thousand attendants in his service.
And from evening until midnight he would indulge in shameful dissipations.
And at midnight he would arise and pray,
surrounded by black eunuchs who were precious to him.
And after prayer he would sit upon his couch
and read in the Gospel until it was day;
and he would mount and go to the service of the Caliph.
It is said
that every night the expense of wax candles, oil, and perfumes was five hundred dinars.
And after he became impoverished,
he left two sons and three daughters,
and wandered dispersed in foreign lands.
And in the year 1170

245 of the Arabs,
an ambassador was sent from Michael, king of the Romans,
an old man named Metrophilos {OCR?}, to al-Mutawakkil, king of the Arabs,
and with him were seventy-seven men from the Arab prisoners;
he brought them as gifts to al-Mutawakkil,
and he was received with honor,
and peace was established.
And in that same year there was a severe earthquake in Antioch,
and it destroyed fifteen hundred houses in it,
and more than ninety towers of its wall.
And terrifying and dreadful voices were heard from within the earth.
And also in all the cities of Syria the earthquake destroyed many places.
(Laodicea and Gabala) For the inhabitants of Laodicea {OCR?} and Gabala perished completely.
